- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is strongly positive (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices during early periods of strong positive sentiment — model reacts too slowly to sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.2), model often undercorrects, failing to anticipate sharp downward moves.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects after strong moves, leading to false peaks or troughs in forecasts.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns sharply, model takes 2–3 days to adjust.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model tends to overforecast, then corrects too late — create a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for each day of sustained positive sentiment.
- For negative sentiment, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day, but cap at 3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting spikes unless sentiment is sustained > 0.7 for 3+ days — otherwise, model overreacts and misses mean reversion.
